# Threat Analysis: JOMANGY — INJ3CTOR3's Self-Healing FreePBX Toll-Fraud Campaign

*Source: Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs (CRIL). Analysis generated by the `threat-report-killchain` skill. Indicators are defanged for safe handling.*

## Executive summary

An active campaign attributed to the long-running VoIP-fraud crew **INJ3CTOR3** (aka INJ3CTOR3S) exploits internet-facing **FreePBX** servers to deploy a previously undocumented PHP webshell family, **JOMANGY**, alongside the **ZenharR** webshell. Access is monetized through **VoIP toll fraud** — the operators originate calls over victims' SIP trunks and stick the victim with the carrier bill. The defining feature is a **six-channel, self-healing persistence architecture** (webshells, cron polling, shell-profile and `rc.local` injection, 18 backdoor accounts, `chattr +i`-immutable crontab backups, and a FreePBX HA `license.php` hook) engineered so that any single surviving component restores all others within minutes — making partial remediation "functionally useless." Likely entry is **CVE-2025-57819** (FreePBX Endpoint pre-auth SQLi) with **CVE-2025-64328** (filestore post-auth RCE) as the prior-campaign vector. Overall attribution confidence is **Medium**; the campaign mechanics and IOCs are documented with **High** confidence.

**Host-based IOCs.** Webshell paths under `/var/www/html/` (incl. `admin/modules/freepbx_ha/license.php`, `admin/views/ajax.php`, `h.php`); persistence files `/root/.bash_profile`, `/root/.bashrc`, `/etc/rc.local`; immutable backup dirs `/var/lib/asterisk/bin/`, `/dev/shm/.systemd/`, `/tmp/.cache/`; C2 web paths `/k.php`, `/x`, `/z/wr.php`, `/z/wor.php`, `/z/post/root.php`, `/z/post/noroot.php`, `___ip.php`, `___ask.php`, `___md5.php`, `___zen.php`; watchdog process names `zen2`, `devnull2`. **Backdoor accounts** — UID-0: `newfpbxs`, `newfpbx`, `xhimax`, `centos`, `admin`, `support`, `issabel`, `sangoma`, `emo`; service: `sugarmaint`, `spamfilter`, `asteriskuser`, `supports`, `freepbxuser`, `supermaint`, `asterisk`, `hima`; web panel: `freepbxusers` (`ampusers`).

## Enrichment findings

- **MITRE ATT&CK (threat actors):** `INJ3CTOR3` → **no matching ATT&CK group**. It is vendor-tracked (Cyble, Fortinet, Unit 42, Check Point) but has no `G`-ID intrusion-set entry, so no ATT&CK-derived technique/software set could be attached. This is a true negative, not a lookup failure.
- **VirusTotal (file hashes):** **Skipped — `VT_API_KEY` not set** (6 full hashes were queued). Per the article's own stated coverage at analysis time: `k.php`/`wr.php` had **0 detections**; the Stage-1 dropper had **4/76**. Set `VT_API_KEY` (and optionally `VT_TIER=premium`) and re-run to populate live verdicts.

## Analyst notes & gaps

- **Truncated hashes in source.** The report publishes only 8-character SHA256 *prefixes* for the seven payload files; these cannot be used for VirusTotal or precise matching. Full hashes exist only for the auth/watermark tokens (MD5) and one MySQL password (SHA1).
- **Hash enrichment not run** (no API key) — see above.
- **INJ3CTOR3 is not an ATT&CK group**; treat attribution as vendor-level, Medium confidence.
- **Reconnaissance and Weaponization** kill-chain phases are inferences (Medium) — the report evidences them indirectly (scanner IP, obfuscation), not as observed operator actions.
- **Windows-only mismaps excluded.** A naive mapping would place shell-profile persistence under `T1547.001` (Registry Run Keys); the host is Linux, so `T1546.004`/`T1037.004` were used instead.
- **Extractor false positives** (`.php`/`.local` filenames caught as domains, vendor site `cyble.com`) were reclassified/dropped during analysis.
